question:
A 74-year-old right-handed woman was referred to the hospital due to concerns of a stroke. In the emergency department, the initial vital signs included blood pressure of 159/98 mm Hg, heart rate of 88/min, and respiratory rate of 20/min. She exhibited paucity of speech and apathy to her condition, although she complied with her physical examination. The initial neurologic evaluation included the following results:
Awake, alert, and oriented to person, place, and time
No visual field deficits
Right-sided gaze deviation with full range of motion with doll’s head maneuver
No facial asymmetry
Grossly intact hearing
No tongue deviation, equal palatal elevation, and good guttural sound production
Absent pronator or lower extremity drift
Decreased sensation to light touch on the right leg
Normal appreciation of light touch, pressure, and pain
Normal proprioception and kinesthesia
Manual muscle testing:
5+ right and left upper extremities
5+ right hip, thigh, leg, and foot
3+ left hip and thigh
2+ left leg and foot
A head computed tomography (CT) scan and a head magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) confirmed areas of ischemia. Which artery is the most likely site of occlusion?

options.opc: Superior division of the right middle cerebral artery
options.opd: Inferior division of the right middle cerebral artery
options.ope: Inferior division of the left middle cerebral artery

nodes: Structure of right middle cerebral artery
Structure of right middle cerebral artery

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Right-sided gaze deviation -> "indicates right hemisphere involvement" -> "suggests occlusion in right cerebral artery" -> "decreased sensation on right leg" -> "consistent with right middle cerebral artery territory" -> "most likely occlusion in right middle cerebral artery stem (M1)" -> 85%

CHAIN: Paucity of speech -> "suggests possible aphasia" -> "indicates left hemisphere involvement" -> "right-sided symptoms suggest right hemisphere occlusion" -> "decreased motor function on left side" -> "consistent with right middle cerebral artery involvement" -> "most likely occlusion in right middle cerebral artery stem (M1)" -> 80%

CHAIN: Areas of ischemia confirmed by CT and MRI -> "indicates recent stroke" -> "right-sided symptoms suggest right hemisphere ischemia" -> "decreased sensation on right leg" -> "consistent with right middle cerebral artery territory" -> "most likely occlusion in right middle cerebral artery stem (M1)" -> 90%

CHAIN: Neurologic evaluation shows intact hearing and no facial asymmetry -> "suggests no brainstem involvement" -> "right-sided gaze deviation indicates right hemisphere issue" -> "decreased sensation on right leg" -> "consistent with right middle cerebral artery territory" -> "most likely occlusion in right middle cerebral artery stem (M1)" -> 80%
enhanced_information: The patient's presentation of right-sided gaze deviation, decreased sensation in the right leg, and motor weakness on the left side suggests right hemisphere involvement, consistent with occlusion in the right middle cerebral artery (MCA) territory. The right MCA supplies the lateral aspect of the cerebral hemisphere, which includes areas responsible for motor and sensory functions of the contralateral side of the body. The neurologic evaluation indicates intact hearing and no facial asymmetry, ruling out brainstem involvement, further supporting the diagnosis of a right MCA occlusion. The imaging findings of ischemia corroborate the clinical assessment. Therefore, the most likely site of occlusion is the right middle cerebral artery stem (M1).
analysis: The patient's clinical presentation indicates a right-sided gaze deviation, decreased sensation in the right leg, and motor weakness on the left side, which suggests a right hemisphere stroke. The right middle cerebral artery (MCA) supplies the lateral aspect of the cerebral hemisphere, including areas responsible for motor and sensory functions of the contralateral side of the body. The absence of facial asymmetry and intact hearing further supports that the brainstem is not involved, which aligns with a right MCA occlusion. Given the options, the right middle cerebral artery stem (M1) is the most likely site of occlusion, as it would affect both motor and sensory functions on the left side of the body, consistent with the observed deficits. Therefore, the best-supported option is the right middle cerebral artery stem (M1).
